result.title: When Order Matters: First-Speaker Bias and Mitigation through Personality in Sequential Multi-Agent Debate
result.summary: Multi-agent debate (MAD) is often used to improve large language model (LLM) reasoning, but sequential debate is rarely a neutral aggregator of agents' opinions. We show that sequential MAD suffers from a pronounced first-speaker bias: agents disproportionately shape the final answer when they speak first. As a result, placing a stronger model after weaker ones can substantially offset its reasoning advantage. We then focus on the disadvantaged strong-agent-last setting and ask whether personality prompting can mitigate this imbalance. Drawing on the Big Five model, we study agreeableness and extraversion as behavioral interventions applied to either the strong or weak side. We find that their effects are trait-specific. Influence consistently shifts in the direction of lower agreeableness, and assigning low agreeableness to the stronger agent helps restore its lost influence and improves final accuracy. Extraversion, by contrast, produces less systematic changes in influence and accuracy, with its clearest effect appearing in agents' verbosity. These findings show that effective MAD design depends not only on model capability, but also on how speaking order and induced interaction behavior shape the debate process.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究顺序式多智能体辩论中的「首位发言者偏差」，发现先发言者的观点对最终答案影响过大，并尝试用大五人格提示（宜人性、外向性）来缓解强模型后发言时的劣势，结果显示低宜人性提示能恢复强智能体的影响力并提升准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为纯文本多智能体辩论、不涉及视觉 latent，但其对「发言顺序决定信息贡献权重」和「贡献分配」的诊断，可供核查多模态推理中证据引入次序与 latent 状态归属是否也存在类似的序位偏差。
